links.outcome: Triage accuracy under exam-style versus naturalistic patient-style evaluation of the same LLMs
links.effect: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points (p = 0.015); asthma triage improved from 48% to 80%; three models scored 0-24% with forced choice but 100% with free text.
links.quote: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points ($p = 0.015$).

links.outcome: Emergency recognition and escalation by consumer LLM chatbots across triage scenarios
links.effect: DKA was triaged correctly in 100% of trials across all models and conditions. Forced-choice format registered under-triage (0-24% for three models) although free text recommended emergency care in 100%.
links.quote: The forced A/B/C/D format was the dominant failure mechanism: three models scored 0--24% with forced choice but 100% with free text (all $p < 10^{-8}$), consistently recommending emergency care in their own words while the forced-choice format registered under-triage.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating consumer health chatbots with free-text, patient-style messages rather than forced-choice exam-style formats
Testing prompt-faithful replication of prior published evaluation scaffolds

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM triage performance under different testing/evaluation formats (forced-choice exam style vs. naturalistic free text), showing benchmark sensitivity rather than testing an operational health care deployment safeguard.
